Express the logarithms using the change‐of‐base formula:
  logₐ(b) = ln(b)/ln(a).

sentence:
Thus, for the kᵗʰ term (with a suitable indexing) we can write:
  log₍ₙ₋ₖ₊₁₎(1/(k+1)) = ln(1/(k+1)) / ln(n–k+1).
sentence-category-reason: Applies the change-of-base to the k-th term with explicit expression.

sentence:
Write each logarithm in terms of natural logarithms:
  ln(1/(k+1)) = –ln(k+1).
sentence-category-reason: Announces rewriting using a logarithm property as the next step.

sentence:
So the kᵗʰ term becomes:
  [– ln(k+1)] / ln(n–k+1).
sentence-category-reason: Carries out the rewrite of the k-th term using the property.

sentence:
Then the whole product becomes:
  P = ∏ₖ₌₁ⁿ⁻¹ [ – ln(k+1) / ln(n–k+1) ].
sentence-category-reason: Forms the whole product in product notation after the rewrite.
A step marker indicating a transition.

sentence:
Factor out (–1) from every term:
  P = (–1)ⁿ⁻¹ · ∏ₖ₌₁ⁿ⁻¹ [ ln(k+1)/ ln(n–k+1) ].
sentence-category-reason: Performs factoring of (−1) from each term and rewrites the product.

sentence:
Observe the structure of the product:
  For k = 1, 2, …, n – 1 the numerator is
   ln(2) · ln(3) · … · ln(n)
  and the denominator is
   ln(n) · ln(n–1) · … · ln(2).
sentence-category-reason: Analyzes the structure of numerators and denominators of the product.

sentence:
Since both products contain the same factors (only in reverse order), their quotient is 1:
  ∏ₖ₌₁ⁿ⁻¹ [ ln(k+1)/ ln(n–k+1) ] = 1.
sentence-category-reason: Draws a logical conclusion that the quotient of matching factors is 1.
